_comment: The shared contract between frontend/ and backend/. Every HTTP route the backend serves under /api is listed here and nothing else; every request the frontend builds targets one of these. tests/contract/routes.test.mjs enforces both directions and fails closed on any path it cannot read as a literal.

routes.doc: Claude CLI login state, node version, data dir.
Taskbar data: recent projects and most-used skills.
Dashboard numbers per project, and what is running now.
Show the Windows folder dialog on this PC and return the chosen path.
Every skill in the local library.
One skill: SKILL.md text and its extra files.
Create or replace a skill's SKILL.md in the library.
Delete a skill from the library (not from projects).
Bump the usage counter behind the taskbar.
List the skills found in a public GitHub repo URL.
Download the picked skills from a GitHub repo into the library.
Import dropped files (a folder or .md) into the library.
Registered projects, recent first.
Register an existing project folder.
Preview (confirm:false) or create a project from a template: writes the rendered files after the diff is confirmed.
Inspect a project: agents, skills, models, engines, roster.
Forget a project (files stay).
Freezes, proposed ADRs, secrets in .mcp.json, git mode, board.
The plan: phases, gates, attached skills and agents, pins.
Save the plan inside the app (no project files written).
Change what Circle Studio may do in a project: change files, run its scripts, send text to Claude.
Read one project file (?path=...), read-only.
Stored chat transcript for a project.
Forget the stored chat transcript and start a new conversation.
Continue a Claude Code conversation from the terminal in this chat ({nodeId?, sessionId}). The first turn forks it.
The Claude Code conversations held in this folder outside the app (read only), and the runs of a node's agent.
One Claude Code conversation (or ?run=agent-x, one subagent run in it) as chat messages, redacted.
Turn edit operations into a diff. Writes nothing.
Apply a previewed change set to the real files.
Stream a turn from the chosen engine in the project folder (server-sent events, including approval and question requests).
Stop a running chat or advisor process.
Ask the claude CLI what to keep, build and fix in a file.
Every engine (claude, codex, gemini, copilot): installed, version, login state, what it can do. No model call.
Re-detect every engine now (bypasses the short cache).
Open a visible terminal that runs one engine's fixed install or sign-in command ({engine, step: install|login}). Nothing typed by the person is run.
The Inbox: approvals and questions agents raised (?status=pending|all&projectId=).
Questions a team's texter raised for the human in docs/tasks/ALERTS.md, across all projects (?status=open|all). Answered by changes.preview/apply with the alert-answer op.
Answer a pending approval or question: allow, deny or answer.
Server-sent events for the whole app: request, request-resolved, run, usage.
Runs in this project right now, per graph node: status, tokens, context, pending requests.
Saved workflow templates.
Create a template: blank, from another template, or from a workflow.
Import a workflow.json (path or pasted JSON) as a new template. Reads that one file only.
One template with its workflow and version history.
Save a template: appends a semantic version.
Delete a template (projects made from it keep their own copy).
A project's workflow graph, its version history and lint warnings.
Save a project's workflow (appends a version) and optionally write files through the diff review.
Restore an older version as a new version.
Ask the workflow helper (Claude, no tools) to answer or propose a better workflow. Writes nothing.
Find skills on GitHub for this workflow (or at the links given): Claude names the gaps, GitHub is searched, Claude picks and explains a few. Imports nothing.
App settings (desktop alerts, update checks) and which app shortcuts exist.
Change app settings: {desktopAlerts?, updates?:{check:"daily"|"off"}}.
Make or remove a Windows shortcut: {where:"desktop"|"startmenu"|"startup", projectId?, remove?}. A project shortcut opens its widget.
Which shortcuts exist, for the app or ?projectId=.
Open an app window: {kind:"app"|"widget", projectId?}.
Read-only git state, and GitHub Actions runs and open pull requests when turned on for the project (?fresh=1 skips the one-minute cache).
Turn GitHub reads on or off for a project: {on}.
Everything a project's widget shows: live runs, pending requests and team questions, workflow stages, git, numbers, the last Claude Code conversation.
Circle Studio's version and the last update check (?check=1 checks the remote now, read only).
Fast-forward the app to its remote (only when its folder is clean and not ahead), then restart it.
What the project costs with Claude Code: context loaded per session, the model of each agent, 30 days of measured usage from its transcripts (priced at API rates), problems and cheaper options.
Ask Circle: {message, engine?} -> matching help topics (no AI) and, unless engine is "none", a read-only answer from the chosen or first signed-in engine.
Use per provider across this PC for ?days=7|30|90: Claude priced at API rates, Codex tokens, Gemini and Copilot turns run from Circle Studio. Cached five minutes (?fresh=1).
MCP servers of every engine (for ?projectId=, its own and the user-level ones; else the whole PC), with names only, never values, and the security findings.
Health of one server: {id, projectId?, remote?}. A remote server is contacted only when remote is true.
The local security check over every project and this PC: connectors, git remotes, tracked secrets, agent settings.
The names in the key vault and where each may be used. Never the values.
Store or update a key: {value?, note?, projects: [ids] | "all"}. Encrypted with Windows DPAPI. Anthropic keys are refused.
Delete a key from the vault.
Move a literal key from a project's .mcp.json into the vault: {projectId, server, field, key, name}; returns the mcp-env-ref op to review.
The building-block catalog (skills, agents, connectors, links), rebuilt when older than 10 minutes; ?q= searches it (BM25), ?type= filters.
Rebuild the catalog from the library, projects, templates and connectors now.
One Haiku call writes short descriptions and tags for up to 40 entries that lack a good one.
Fetch one https page once ({url}) and keep its text in chunks so it can be retrieved (the helper's RAG).
The desktop widgets' tiles, ready to draw (text, rings, rows, bars), with the tokens.css palette for ?theme=dark|light.
Start, stop or ask about the native desktop widgets: {action: "start"|"stop"|"status"}.
Start one MCP server for real and do the handshake: {id, projectId?} -> result, plain-words diagnosis with fixes, its output (redacted).

Claude reads the failed test, the server config (names only) and its code, and answers: cause, steps, safe commands, a config fix (as an mcp-server-set op for a project .mcp.json) and advice for the codebase.

Every MCP server grouped by name across projects and engines, with what is redundant (copies, conflicting setups, folders that are gone), broken or holding a plain-text key, and a one-click fix for each.
Preview a fix: {action: {kind: repair|share|remove|secure|key, ...}, projectId?} -> plain steps and commands, never a key value.
Run a previewed fix (~/.claude.json backed up first and put back on failure), then test the servers it touched. Project .mcp.json changes come back as ops to review.
